newsitem.title: COMOROS: Secessionists man roadblocks on Comoro island.
newsitem.headline: Secessionists man roadblocks on Comoro island.

text.p: Secessionists pulled down Comoran flags, raised the red flag of an 18th-century sultan and set up roadblocks on the Indian Ocean island of Anjouan on Thursday, witnesses said.

They said the island was brought to a standstill for a second consecutive day by protesters setting up roadblocks and burning tyres on the road from the main airport on Anjouan to the regional capital of Mutsamulu.
Businesses and government offices remained closed.
"The situation is dangerously out of control," an expatriate on Anjouan told Reuters by telephone to Moroni, capital of the Comoros, an archipelago of four small islands in the Indian Ocean.
Witnesses said supporters of secession for Anjouan from the other islands pulled down the Comoran flag in the main square in Mutsamulu and raised the red flag of an 18th-century sultan of the island.
On Wednesday, security forces tried to bring the situation under control and two civilians were wounded by bullets.

State radio has made no mention of the events on Anjouan, which has a population of about 190,000 and is 130 km (80 miles) southeast of the main island of Grande-Comore and 450 km (280 miles) northwest of the island state of Madagascar.
The Comoro Islands have been swept this year by a series of strikes by civil servants demanding payment of their salaries.
Teachers and hospital staff have been on strike since the start of the year, initially demanding payment of 10 months of salaries owed by the government of the coup-prone archipelago.

President Mohamed Taki's government blames its failure to pay civil servants on the disastrous state of public finances. The Comoros have had up to 17 attempted coups since independence from France in 1975.
